chunks: Abu Ishaq Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Hamzah ibn Ammarah al-Hafiz informed me in what he wrote to me, saying: Salim ibn Salim and Abu Arooba narrated to me, saying: Abul-Khattab narrated to me, saying: Harun ibn Muslim narrated to me, saying: Al-Qasim ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Ansari narrated to me, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from his father, from al-Hussein ibn Ali (peace be upon them).

He said: When the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) conquered Khaybar, he called for his bow and leaned on its handle. Then he praised Allah and extolled Him, and mentioned what Allah had opened for him and granted him victory through. He forbade nine things: the dowry of the fornicatress; the rental of the beast of burden (meaning the mating fee of the male); wearing a gold ring; the price of the dog; and violet saddles. Abu Arooba said: red saddles; wearing clothes called 'al-Qasi' which are woven in Syria; eating the meat of beasts of prey; exchanging gold with gold and silver with silver where there is a surplus between them; and gazing at the stars.

key_terms.عَسَبَ الْفَحْلِ: Mating fee of the male beast

ai.seo_question: What are the nine things the Prophet forbade after the conquest of Khaybar?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal*, this hadith highlights the Prophet’s (peace be upon him) post-conquest admonition, linking material prohibitions to spiritual purity and economic justice. The inclusion of 'gazing at the stars' (al-nazar fi al-nujum) specifically points to the pre-Islamic practice of astrology, distinguishing it from general astronomy, while the rules on gold and silver exchange reinforce the prohibition of *riba* (usury) in commodity trading. This collection serves as a practical guide for Shia jurisprudence, illustrating how the Prophet’s specific rulings on daily life reflect broader ethical principles.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 9-10 Abu Ishaq Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Hamzih ibn Am’marat al-Hafiz said in what he wrote me that Salim ibn Salim and Abu Aroobat narrated that Abul-Khat’tab quoted Harun ibn Muslim, on the authority of Al-Qasim ibn Abdul Rahman al-Ansari, on the authority of Abdul Rahman al-Ansari, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (MGB), on the authority of his father (MGB), on the authority of Al-Hussein ibn Ali (MGB), “When the Prophet (MGB) conquered the Fort at Khaybar, he (MGB) asked them to fetch his bow and leaned on its handle.

Then he praised God and recited God’s glorifications. He mentioned that God had brought this victory and triumph. Then the Prophet (MGB) admonished us against doing nine things: dowry of the fornicatress ; renting a male quadruped to copulate with female quadrupeds; wearing gold rings (for men); money paid for buying dogs; and violet saddles for riding animals (which Abu Aroobat has said, ‘red saddles’); wearing certain clothes called Al-Qasi which were made in Syria; eating the meat of beasts of prey; exchanging some gold with more gold and silver with more silver ; and looking at the stars.”
